recommendedCorpus.title: DictionaryRoot Core Lexical Corpus v1
recommendedCorpus.selectionMethod: Deterministic stratified sampling from a reviewed candidate ledger, keyed by normalized lemma and strata rather than alphabetic convenience.
strata: historical, obsolete, technical, and variant senses
future BibleRoot translation, metaphor, idiom, and semantic-range cases

mandatoryMinimum.condition: Feasible only after approval of a narrow lexical-claim/form/locator/provenance/comparison schema extension and matching API contract.

lexicalModelCapabilities.rationale: Node metadata and lemma arrays can retain written forms, but form identity is not first-class.
normalized_lemmas is indexed in the DictionaryRoot lexical table.
Each lexical synset row and node ID represents a sense-like lexical concept.
The lexical table has one definition column; multiple source claims need separate claim identity and source joins.
part_of_speech is stored, indexed through queries, and displayed.
Synset type and generic metadata can retain categories.
Generic assertion/node metadata can carry labels, but the complete index and UI do not expose them.
WordNet domain relations exist; normalized label claims need generator/service additions.
Can be source-backed metadata but is not modeled or displayed today.
Durable source-backed status, period, and provenance need structured claim fields.
A boolean alone would lose source, date, and qualification.
Technical domains can be source-backed metadata pending UI activation.
Forms need stable identity, grammatical features, and source provenance.
DERIVATIONALLY_RELATED_TO edges exist, though form-vs-sense semantics need review.
Can be represented as a typed lexical relation after deterministic modeling rules.
Shared sense membership can express synonymy without manufacturing pairwise claims.
ANTONYM_OF is an existing typed relation.
Hypernym relations and generic typed edges support broader concepts.
Hyponym relations and generic typed edges support narrower concepts.
Generic typed edges and ALSO_SEE are supported.
Variant identity, type, period, dialect, and provenance need a form model.
The contextual alias model is not connected to DictionaryRoot lexical senses.
Needs language identity plus sourced/qualified claims.
Needs first-class etymon/form identity and directed provenance.
Requires chronological sense relations and evidence, not a generic edge label alone.
Competing proposals, qualifiers, sources, and review state must remain distinct.
Examples are stored and exposed as usage-example assertions.
Can be source-backed metadata, but no current importer/API/UI contract exposes it.
Nodes, assertions, and edges carry source IDs.
Context locators exist but are evidence-scoped and not linked to lexical claims.
Context field provenance exists but is not connected to DictionaryRoot lexical fields.
Generic revisions and the History customer experience preserve explicit snapshots.
No structure links distinct source statements to one reviewed sense with a comparison decision.

apiFindings.requirement: exact lemma search, sense resolution, definition assertions, edges, source records, and revision history
multi-source definition claims, form records, etymology proposals, source locators, field provenance, and comparison decisions
bounded pagination/facets for larger sense and source-comparison result sets

migrationFindings: Migration 013 remains absent during this gate.

Production implementation requires approval for first-class lexical claims, forms, etymology proposals, locators, field provenance, and source comparisons, or an equally explicit reviewed alternative.
Generic JSON metadata alone is insufficient for durable field-level provenance and competing source statements.

sourceComparisonPlan.rule: Lexical identity, part of speech, time/domain labels, and inspectible source statements drive a deterministic candidate comparison; a human records the accepted decision and rationale.
sourceComparisonPlan.algorithmicSimilarity: Permitted only as a review queue aid; never stored as the accepted comparison decision.

reviewFindings: Wiktionary and DBnary are one editorial lineage and must not count as independent corroboration.
Princeton WordNet and OEWN are related editions and must carry an explicit lineage relation.
Historical OCR and transcription must be checked against page images before claim acceptance.
NIST aggregated definitions require item-level source-publication and rights validation.
Thesaurus co-membership and ConceptNet relatedness are discovery signals, not accepted synonymy.
observations: The repository pilot already proves multiple senses, exact search, source attribution, examples, and typed semantic relations.
The live test database currently contains no DictionaryRoot lexicon dataset row, so repository and database baselines differ.
The current customer experience already renders sense choice, part of speech, definitions, word forms, relationships, sources, and revision links.
unresolvedRightsQuestions: Confirm international public-domain treatment before distribution outside the United States.
Approve license-layer isolation policy for CC BY-SA/GFDL-derived text.
Perform item-level review for government vocabularies containing third-party contributions.
unresolvedModelingQuestions: Approve first-class form and etymology proposal identities.
Approve sense alignment and source-comparison review states.
Choose whether phrase-level semantics share the lexical schema or a later BibleRoot extension.
unresolvedSourceAccessQuestions: Pin exact archive items and checksums for each historical volume during implementation.
Confirm rate and download policies immediately before acquisition.
unresolvedFrontendQuestions: Choose comparison layout and uncertainty-label vocabulary.
Choose pagination/facet behavior for dense polysemy and larger search results.
unresolvedApiQuestions: Define read contracts for claims, forms, etymology proposals, locators, provenance, and comparisons.
unresolvedMigrationQuestions: Migration 013 or a later approved migration is required for the recommended normalized model.

recommendation.rationale: The accepted source set exceeds all category thresholds and can support every mandatory minimum without copyrighted modern definition reproduction, but the current schema/API cannot preserve required claim, form, locator, provenance, etymology, and comparison distinctions without a narrow approved extension.
conditions: Approve API contracts and targeted frontend enhancements before production import.
Run page-image and item-level rights review during source preparation.
